source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וַיַּכְנִיעֵ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־מֶ֥תֶג הָאַמָּ֖ה מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after thus, and struck David [the] Philistines and subdued them, and took David Metheg-ammah from [the] hand of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And it was after this, and David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah from [the] hand of the Philistines.
en.B: Some time after this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Metheg-ammah out of the Philistines' hands.
en.R: Later David defeated the Philistines and made them give in to him. He took Metheg-ammah away from the Philistines.

fr.L: Et il arriva après cela que David frappa les Philistins et les abaissa, et David prit Métheg-Amma de la main des Philistins.
fr.B: Quelque temps après, David battit les Philistins et les soumit. Il enleva Métheg-Amma aux mains des Philistins.
fr.R: Plus tard, David a battu les Philistins et les a obligés à se soumettre. Il a pris Métheg-Amma aux Philistins.

decisions.choice: after this: a loose link to what comes before, not a precise date
decisions.reason: The chapter gathers David's wars into one summary. "After this" joins it to chapter 7 without claiming that every battle came after Nathan's message; some, such as the wars with Ammon in chapters 10-12, are told at length later.

decisions.choice: Metheg-ammah: a place name whose meaning is not known
alternatives: took control of the chief city
took the bridle of the mother city
decisions.reason: The words can be read as "the bridle of the cubit" or "the bridle of the mother city", which some take as a picture of taking control of the Philistines' chief city. Neither reading is clear, and the phrase is kept as a name. 1 Chronicles 18:1 tells the same event as David taking "Gath and its villages", Gath being one of the five main Philistine cities.

decisions.choice: from the hand of the Philistines: from their control
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The Philistines, who had pressed Israel since the days of Samson and Saul (1 Samuel 31:1-7), now lose ground to David, as 5:17-25 began.

decisions.choice: brought them under his control (Balanced); made them give in to him (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble or bring low; both levels say plainly that the Philistines were made to submit.

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־מוֹאָ֗ב וַֽיְמַדְּדֵ֤ם בַּחֶ֨בֶל֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ב אוֹתָ֣ם אַ֔רְצָה וַיְמַדֵּ֤ד שְׁנֵֽי־חֲבָלִים֙ לְהָמִ֔ית וּמְלֹ֥א הַחֶ֖בֶל לְהַחֲי֑וֹת וַתְּהִ֤י מוֹאָב֙ לְדָוִ֔ד לַעֲבָדִ֖ים נֹשְׂאֵ֥י מִנְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck Moab, and measured them with the line, making lie them [on the] ground, and measured two lines to put to death and [the] fullness of the line to keep alive; and became Moab to David [as] servants bearing tribute.

en.L: And he struck Moab, and he measured them with the line, making them lie down [on the] ground; and he measured two lines to put to death and a full line to keep alive. And Moab became servants to David, bearing tribute.
en.B: He also defeated Moab. He had the Moabites lie down on the ground and used a cord to measure them off: two lengths of cord were to be put to death and one full length kept alive. So the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute.
en.R: David also defeated the Moabites. He made the prisoners lie down on the ground in rows and measured them with a rope. He had two rope lengths of them killed, and he let one full length of them live. So the Moabites came under David's rule and paid him tribute.

fr.L: Et il frappa Moab, et il les mesura au cordeau, en les faisant coucher à terre ; et il mesura deux cordeaux pour faire mourir et un plein cordeau pour laisser vivre. Et Moab devint pour David des serviteurs portant tribut.
fr.B: Il battit aussi Moab. Il fit coucher les Moabites à terre et les mesura au cordeau : deux longueurs de cordeau devaient être mises à mort, et une pleine longueur laissée en vie. Ainsi les Moabites furent soumis à David et lui payèrent un tribut.
fr.R: David a aussi battu les Moabites. Il a fait coucher les prisonniers par terre en rangs et il les a mesurés avec une corde. Il a fait tuer deux longueurs de corde, et il a laissé en vie une longueur entière. Ainsi les Moabites sont passés sous l’autorité de David et lui ont payé un tribut.

decisions.choice: the captives were measured off with a cord: two lengths killed, one length spared
decisions.reason: David has the Moabite prisoners lie down in rows and uses a measuring cord to decide who dies. The cord is a builder's or surveyor's line, of no fixed length. On the plain reading two parts in three were killed and one part spared; the "full line" may mean a whole length, slightly favoring the group that lived. The text does not say why David dealt so harshly with Moab, though he had once trusted his parents to the king of Moab (1 Samuel 22:3-4). 1 Chronicles 18:2 reports the victory without the measuring.

decisions.choice: servants bearing tribute: a subject people paying regular tribute
decisions.reason: Servants here means a nation under David's rule, not slaves in households. The word for tribute is the one used for a grain offering; here it is the gift a subject king brings his overlord (Judges 3:15-18).

decisions.choice: the Moabites (Balanced); the Moabites, the prisoners (Readable)
decisions.reason: Moab is the nation, and "them" in the measuring are its captured soldiers. Balanced and Readable name the people, and Readable says they were prisoners and that they lay "in rows", which the measuring by lengths of cord implies.

decisions.choice: became subject to David (Balanced); came under David's rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: For a whole nation "servants" means subjects; Literal keeps the word "servants".

decisions.choice: des serviteurs (L); soumis à David (B); sous l'autorité de David (R)
decisions.reason: For a whole nation "servants" means subjects (m2), as the English says at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "serviteurs".

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ דָּוִ֔ד אֶת־הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר בֶּן־רְחֹ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ צוֹבָ֑ה בְּלֶכְתּ֕וֹ לְהָשִׁ֥יב יָד֖וֹ בִּֽנְהַר־פְּרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck David Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, in his going to restore his hand at [the] river Euphrates.

en.L: And David struck Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his hand at the river Euphrates.
en.B: David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when Hadadezer went to restore his control at the Euphrates River.
en.R: David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, the king of Zobah. This happened when Hadadezer was going to take back control of the land along the Euphrates River.

fr.L: Et David frappa Hadadézer fils de Rehob, roi de Soba, alors qu’il allait rétablir sa main sur le fleuve Euphrate.
fr.B: David battit aussi Hadadézer fils de Rehob, roi de Soba, alors qu’Hadadézer allait rétablir son pouvoir sur l’Euphrate.
fr.R: David a aussi battu Hadadézer fils de Rehob, le roi de Soba. Cela s’est passé quand Hadadézer allait reprendre le contrôle du pays le long de l’Euphrate.

decisions.choice: Hadadezer king of Zobah: ruler of an Aramean kingdom north of Damascus
decisions.reason: Zobah was the strongest of the Aramean (Syrian) kingdoms of the time, in the valley between the Lebanon ranges, north of Damascus. Saul had fought its kings (1 Samuel 14:47). The name Hadadezer means "Hadad is help", Hadad being the storm god of the Arameans.

decisions.choice: he: Hadadezer, on his way to the Euphrates
alternatives: David, going to set up his own power at the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "as he went". The nearer person is Hadadezer, and 10:16 shows him with interests beyond the Euphrates, so he is the one setting out. It could also mean David, going to set up his own power at the river, which would fit the promise of land to the Euphrates (Genesis 15:18).

decisions.choice: restore his hand: take back his power, or set up again his monument
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, and "restore his hand" means to re-establish control. The same word can name a victory monument (1 Samuel 15:12; 2 Samuel 18:18), and 1 Chronicles 18:3 says "set up his hand", which could mean a memorial pillar. Either way, he was asserting his rule along the river.

decisions.choice: the river Euphrates
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has only "the river"; the Jewish scribes' reading tradition adds "Euphrates", as 1 Chronicles 18:3 has it. "The river" on its own often means the Euphrates (Genesis 31:21), so the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: when Hadadezer went
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Hadadezer for "he", following meaning decision m2; Literal keeps the bare pronoun.

source.text: וַיִּלְכֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֜ד מִמֶּ֗נּוּ אֶ֤לֶף וּשְׁבַע־מֵאוֹת֙ פָּרָשִׁ֔ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ רַגְלִ֑י וַיְעַקֵּ֤ר דָּוִד֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָרֶ֔כֶב וַיּוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מֵ֥אָה רָֽכֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And captured David from him 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 man [on] foot; and hamstrung David all the chariotry, and left from it a hundred chariot[s].

en.L: And David captured from him 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 men on foot. And David hamstrung all the chariot [horses], and he left of them a hundred chariot[s].
en.B: David captured 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He hamstrung all the chariot horses but kept enough of them for a hundred chariots.
en.R: David captured 1,700 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers. He crippled all the chariot horses so that they could not be used in battle, except for enough to pull a hundred chariots.

fr.L: Et David lui prit 1 700 cavaliers et 20 000 hommes à pied. Et David coupa les jarrets de tous les [chevaux de] chars, et il en laissa cent char[s].
fr.B: David lui prit 1 700 cavaliers et 20 000 fantassins. Il coupa les jarrets de tous les chevaux de char, mais il en garda assez pour cent chars.
fr.R: David a capturé 1 700 cavaliers et 20 000 soldats à pied. Il a coupé les jarrets de tous les chevaux de char pour qu’ils ne puissent plus servir à la guerre, sauf ce qu’il fallait pour tirer cent chars.

decisions.choice: 1,700 horsemen
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:4 reads "1,000 chariots and 7,000 horsemen" and the Greek translation of Samuel agrees with it. The Hebrew of Samuel may have lost the word "chariots" in copying, so that "a thousand [chariots] and seven thousand horsemen" became "1,700 horsemen". The Hebrew text is followed here. On the size of "thousand" in such counts, see the note at Numbers 1.

decisions.choice: hamstrung the chariot horses: cut the tendons of their hind legs so they could not run
decisions.reason: "Chariotry" here means the horses that drew the chariots. Joshua did the same at the LORD's command (Joshua 11:6, 9). Israel's kings were not to build up great numbers of horses (Deuteronomy 17:16), and David keeps only enough for a hundred chariots.

decisions.choice: chariot [horses]; enough of them for a hundred chariots
decisions.reason: "Left a hundred chariots" means he spared the horses for them. Literal brackets "horses"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly, and Readable adds what hamstringing did.

decisions.choice: 1 700, 20 000 in figures, with a non-breaking space for thousands
decisions.reason: French writes large numbers in figures, thousands set off by a space, as the French style guide and the Pentateuch terms list set.

source.text: וַתָּבֹא֙ אֲרַ֣ם דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק לַעְזֹ֕ר לַהֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ צוֹבָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ דָּוִד֙ בַּֽאֲרָ֔ם עֶשְׂרִֽים־וּשְׁנַ֥יִם אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Aram [of] Damascus to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and struck David among Aram twenty and two thousand man.

en.L: And Aram of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck down among Aram 22,000 men.
en.B: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down 22,000 of the Arameans.
en.R: The Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, the king of Zobah. But David killed 22,000 of them.

fr.L: Et Aram de Damas vint au secours d’Hadadézer roi de Soba, et David abattit parmi Aram 22 000 hommes.
fr.B: Quand les Araméens de Damas vinrent au secours d’Hadadézer, roi de Soba, David abattit 22 000 Araméens.
fr.R: Les Araméens de Damas sont venus aider Hadadézer, le roi de Soba. Mais David en a tué 22 000.

decisions.choice: Aram of Damascus: the Aramean kingdom centered on the city of Damascus
decisions.reason: Aram is the land and people of the Arameans, in what is now Syria. Damascus was then one Aramean state among several, south of Zobah; later it became Israel's chief enemy to the north (1 Kings 20; 2 Kings 8).

decisions.choice: struck down: killed in battle
decisions.reason: The verb used throughout the chapter can mean to defeat or to strike dead. With a count of men it means that many fell.

decisions.choice: the Arameans
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people rather than the land, as the Hebrew does when it says Aram became David's servants in the next verse.

source.text: וַיָּ֨שֶׂם דָּוִ֤ד נְצִבִים֙ בַּאֲרַ֣ם דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַתְּהִ֤י אֲרָם֙ לְדָוִ֔ד לַעֲבָדִ֖ים נוֹשְׂאֵ֣י מִנְחָ֑ה וַיֹּ֤שַׁע יְהוָה֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And put David garrisons in Aram [of] Damascus, and became Aram to David [as] servants bearing tribute; and saved Yahweh David in all that he went.

en.L: And David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and Aram became servants to David, bearing tribute. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved David wherever he went.
en.B: Then David stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus. The Arameans became David's subjects and paid him tribute. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave David victory wherever he went.
en.R: Then David put groups of soldiers in the Aramean lands around Damascus. The Arameans came under David's rule and paid him tribute. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made David win wherever he went.

fr.L: Et David mit des garnisons dans Aram de Damas, et Aram devint pour David des serviteurs portant tribut. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sauva David partout où il alla.
fr.B: Puis David plaça des garnisons dans l’Aram de Damas. Les Araméens furent soumis à David et lui payèrent un tribut. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donna la victoire à David partout où il alla.
fr.R: Ensuite David a installé des groupes de soldats dans les régions araméennes autour de Damas. Les Araméens sont passés sous l’autorité de David et lui ont payé un tribut. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait gagner David partout où il allait.

decisions.choice: garrisons: posts of soldiers holding the land
decisions.reason: The word means something set or stationed. It can name a garrison of troops (1 Samuel 13:3) or an official set over a district (1 Kings 4:5, 7). Either way David now controls Aram of Damascus.

decisions.choice: servants bearing tribute: as in verse 2
decisions.reason: As with Moab in verse 2, Aram becomes a subject people paying tribute.

decisions.choice: the LORD saved David: the victories are the LORD's doing
decisions.reason: The verb is the common word for saving or rescuing; here it means giving victory. The writer credits the LORD with all of David's success, as he promised in 7:9 ("I have cut off all your enemies"). The same sentence closes verse 14.

decisions.choice: gave David victory (Balanced); made David win (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "saved"; in a battle the sense is victory, and Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח דָּוִ֗ד אֵ֚ת שִׁלְטֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֔וּ אֶ֖ל עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר וַיְבִיאֵ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took David the shields of the gold which were on [the] servants of Hadadezer, and brought them [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's officials had carried, and brought them to Jerusalem.
en.R: Hadadezer's officers had carried shields made of gold. David took them and brought them to Jerusalem.

fr.L: Et David prit les boucliers d’or qui étaient sur les serviteurs d’Hadadézer, et les apporta [à] Jérusalem.
fr.B: David prit les boucliers d’or que portaient les officiers d’Hadadézer et les apporta à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Les officiers d’Hadadézer portaient des boucliers en or. David les a pris et il les a apportés à Jérusalem.

decisions.choice: shields: probably shields, perhaps quivers or other gear for display
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its exact sense is uncertain. It names objects hung on walls or carried by guards (Song of Songs 4:4; Ezekiel 27:11), and it was later kept in the temple (2 Kings 11:10). Shields are the most likely sense; gold ones would have been for display rather than battle.

decisions.choice: servants of Hadadezer: his officials or officers
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his court officials and commanders, the men of rank who carried such shields.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced); officers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere for a king's "servants", Balanced uses "officials"; Readable says "officers" because they carried shields.

source.text: וּמִבֶּ֥טַח וּמִבֵּֽרֹתַ֖י עָרֵ֣י הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר לָקַ֞ח הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד נְחֹ֖שֶׁת הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, took the king David bronze much very.

en.L: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took very much bronze.
en.B: From Betah and Berothai, towns of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.
en.R: King David also took a large amount of bronze from Betah and Berothai, two of Hadadezer's towns.

fr.L: Et de Béta et de Bérotaï, villes d’Hadadézer, le roi David prit du bronze en très grande quantité.
fr.B: À Béta et à Bérotaï, villes d’Hadadézer, le roi David prit une grande quantité de bronze.
fr.R: Le roi David a aussi pris beaucoup de bronze à Béta et à Bérotaï, deux villes d’Hadadézer.

decisions.choice: Betah and Berothai
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:8 names the towns Tibhath and Cun. Betah and Tibhath may be one name written differently. Berothai is probably the Berothah of Ezekiel 47:16, on the northern edge of the land.

decisions.choice: very much bronze
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:8 adds that Solomon later used this bronze to make the bronze sea, the pillars and the bronze vessels of the temple (1 Kings 7:15-47).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֕ע תֹּ֖עִי מֶ֣לֶךְ חֲמָ֑ת כִּ֚י הִכָּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל־חֵ֥יל הֲדַדְעָֽזֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Toi king of Hamath that struck David all [the] army of Hadadezer,

en.L: And Toi king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer,
en.B: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer,
en.R: Toi, the king of Hamath, heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army.

fr.L: Et Toï, roi de Hamath, apprit que David avait frappé toute l’armée d’Hadadézer,
fr.B: Quand Toï, roi de Hamath, apprit que David avait battu toute l’armée d’Hadadézer,
fr.R: Toï, le roi de Hamath, a appris que David avait battu toute l’armée d’Hadadézer.

decisions.choice: Toi king of Hamath: ruler of a kingdom north of Zobah
decisions.reason: Hamath lay on the Orontes River, north of Zobah, and later marked the northern limit of Israel's land ("Lebo-hamath", Numbers 34:8; 1 Kings 8:65). 1 Chronicles 18:9 spells the king's name Tou.

decisions.choice: one sentence running into verse 10
decisions.reason: Verse 9 says what Toi heard and verse 10 what he did about it; together they form one sentence.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח תֹּ֣עִי אֶת־יֽוֹרָם־בְּנ֣וֹ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־דָּ֠וִד לִשְׁאָל־ל֨וֹ לְשָׁל֜וֹם וּֽלְבָרֲכ֗וֹ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִלְחַ֤ם בַּהֲדַדְעֶ֨זֶר֙ וַיַּכֵּ֔הוּ כִּי־אִ֛ישׁ מִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תֹּ֖עִי הָיָ֣ה הֲדַדְעָ֑זֶר וּבְיָד֗וֹ הָי֛וּ כְּלֵֽי־כֶ֥סֶף וּכְלֵֽי־זָהָ֖ב וּכְלֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: and sent Toi Joram his son to the king David to ask to him for peace and to bless him because that he fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for [a] man of wars [of] Toi was Hadadezer; and in his hand were articles of silver and articles of gold and articles of bronze.

en.L: and Toi sent Joram his son to King David to ask him about [his] peace and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him, for Hadadezer had been a man of wars [with] Toi. And in his hand were articles of silver and articles of gold and articles of bronze.
en.B: he sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on fighting against Hadadezer and defeating him, for Hadadezer and Toi had often been at war. Joram brought articles of silver, gold and bronze with him.
en.R: So he sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and to congratulate him for fighting Hadadezer and defeating him. Hadadezer had been at war with Toi many times. Joram brought gifts made of silver, gold and bronze.

fr.L: et Toï envoya Joram son fils au roi David pour lui demander [comment il allait] et pour le bénir, parce qu’il avait combattu contre Hadadézer et l’avait frappé, car Hadadézer était un homme en guerre [avec] Toï. Et dans sa main il y avait des objets d’argent, et des objets d’or, et des objets de bronze.
fr.B: il envoya son fils Joram au roi David pour le saluer et le féliciter d’avoir combattu Hadadézer et de l’avoir battu, car Hadadézer et Toï étaient souvent en guerre. Joram apporta avec lui des objets d’argent, d’or et de bronze.
fr.R: Alors il a envoyé son fils Joram auprès du roi David pour le saluer et le féliciter d’avoir combattu et battu Hadadézer. Hadadézer avait souvent fait la guerre contre Toï. Joram a apporté des cadeaux en argent, en or et en bronze.

decisions.choice: ask him about his peace: greet him, ask after his well-being
decisions.reason: To "ask someone of peace" is the usual way of greeting (Genesis 43:27; 1 Samuel 17:22). Coming from one king to another it is also a request for good relations.

decisions.choice: bless him: congratulate him, wish him well
decisions.reason: Between people, to bless can mean to praise or congratulate someone on success, as here on David's victory.

decisions.choice: a man of wars of Toi: one who was often at war with Toi
decisions.reason: The phrase makes Hadadezer Toi's regular enemy. David's victory freed Toi from a dangerous neighbor, which is why his gifts are generous.

decisions.choice: Joram
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:10 calls the son Hadoram. The two names differ in the god they honor: Joram contains a short form of the LORD's name, and Hadoram the name of the Aramean god Hadad. The prince may have had both names, or the name may have been changed in the telling at David's court.

decisions.choice: Joram brought with him
decisions.reason: "In his hand were" means he brought these as gifts. Balanced and Readable say so and name Joram, and Readable calls the articles gifts.

source.text: גַּם־אֹתָ֕ם הִקְדִּ֛ישׁ הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד לַֽיהוָ֑ה עִם־הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְהַזָּהָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדִּ֔ישׁ מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר כִּבֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Also them dedicated the king David to Yahweh with the silver and the gold which he dedicated from all the nations which he subdued,

en.L: These also King David dedicated to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with the silver and the gold that he had dedicated from all the nations that he had subdued:
en.B: King David dedicated these also to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as he had done with the silver and gold taken from all the nations he had brought under his control:
en.R: King David gave these gifts to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} too, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations he had conquered.

fr.L: Ceux-là aussi, le roi David les consacra {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, avec l’argent et l’or qu’il avait consacrés de toutes les nations qu’il avait soumises :
fr.B: Le roi David les consacra eux aussi {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, comme il l’avait fait de l’argent et de l’or pris à toutes les nations qu’il avait soumises :
fr.R: Le roi David a aussi donné ces cadeaux {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, avec l’argent et l’or qu’il avait pris à toutes les nations qu’il avait vaincues.

decisions.choice: dedicated: set apart as holy, given over for the LORD's use
decisions.reason: The verb means to make holy. The metal became the LORD's property, to be kept for his house; 1 Chronicles 18:8 and 1 Kings 7:51 say it was later used in and stored in Solomon's temple.

decisions.choice: the spoils go to the LORD
decisions.reason: David does not keep the plunder for himself but gives it to the LORD, who gave him the victories (verses 6 and 14). The gift also fits his wish to build a house for the LORD (7:2).

decisions.choice: the sentence continues into verse 12, which lists the nations
decisions.reason: Verse 12 names the nations from which the silver and gold came, so verse 11 ends with a colon at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: the silver and gold he had taken from ... he had conquered
decisions.reason: Readable says the silver and gold was taken from the nations, which is what "dedicated from all the nations" means.

source.text: מֵאֲרָ֤ם וּמִמּוֹאָב֙ וּמִבְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וּמִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וּמֵֽעֲמָלֵ֑ק וּמִשְּׁלַ֛ל הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר בֶּן־רְחֹ֖ב מֶ֥לֶךְ צוֹבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: from Aram and from Moab and from [the] sons of Ammon and from [the] Philistines and from Amalek, and from [the] plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

en.L: from Aram and from Moab and from the sons of Ammon and from the Philistines and from Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
en.B: from Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and Amalek, and from the plunder taken from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
en.R: These nations were Aram, Moab, Ammon, Philistia and Amalek. He also gave the things he had taken from Hadadezer son of Rehob, the king of Zobah.

fr.L: d’Aram, et de Moab, et des fils d’Ammon, et des Philistins, et d’Amalek, et du butin d’Hadadézer fils de Rehob, roi de Soba.
fr.B: d’Aram, de Moab, des Ammonites, des Philistins et d’Amalek, et du butin pris à Hadadézer fils de Rehob, roi de Soba.
fr.R: Ces nations étaient Aram, Moab, Ammon, les Philistins et Amalek. Il a aussi donné ce qu’il avait pris à Hadadézer fils de Rehob, le roi de Soba.

decisions.choice: Aram
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:11, the Greek translation and the Syriac read "Edom". In Hebrew script the two names differ by one letter that is easily confused. Edom is otherwise missing from this list, though verse 14 tells of its conquest, while Aram already appears through Hadadezer at the end of the verse. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Ammon and Amalek: wars told elsewhere
decisions.reason: David's war with Ammon is told in chapters 10-12, and his fight with the Amalekites in 1 Samuel 30. This verse gathers the spoils of his whole reign.

decisions.choice: the sons of Ammon
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of Ammon", the Hebrew way of naming the people of Ammon, as in chapters 10-12. Balanced and Readable say "the Ammonites" or "Ammon", which needs no setting.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ דָּוִד֙ שֵׁ֔ם בְּשֻׁב֕וֹ מֵהַכּוֹת֥וֹ אֶת־אֲרָ֖ם בְּגֵיא־מֶ֑לַח שְׁמוֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אָֽלֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And made David [a] name in his returning from his striking Aram in [the] Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand.

en.L: And David made a name [for himself] when he returned from striking down Aram in the Valley of Salt, 18,000 [men].
en.B: David made a name for himself when he came back from striking down 18,000 Arameans in the Valley of Salt.
en.R: David became famous after he came back from killing 18,000 Arameans in the Valley of Salt.

fr.L: Et David se fit un nom quand il revint d’avoir frappé Aram dans la vallée du Sel, 18 000 [hommes].
fr.B: David se fit un nom à son retour, après avoir abattu 18 000 Araméens dans la vallée du Sel.
fr.R: David est devenu célèbre quand il est revenu après avoir tué 18 000 Araméens dans la vallée du Sel.

decisions.choice: made a name: won fame
decisions.reason: To make a name is to gain a lasting reputation. The LORD had promised David "a great name" (7:9), and the victories bring it about.

decisions.choice: Aram
alternatives: returned from striking Aram, he struck Edom in the Valley of Salt
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:12 and the Greek translation read "Edom", and the title of Psalm 60 (60:2) speaks of 12,000 of Edom struck in the Valley of Salt. The Valley of Salt lies near Edom, south of the Dead Sea (2 Kings 14:7), and verse 14 goes on to Edom. Aram and Edom differ by one easily confused letter in Hebrew. Another possibility is that words have dropped out, and the verse once said that after striking Aram David struck Edom in the Valley of Salt. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: 18,000: the same battle as Psalm 60's title and 1 Chronicles 18:12
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:12 credits the victory to Abishai son of Zeruiah, and the title of Psalm 60 to Joab with 12,000 killed. Here David, as king, is credited with the victory his commanders won.

decisions.choice: a name [for himself]; 18,000 [men]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs; Balanced and Readable turn the number into "18,000 Arameans".

source.text: וַיָּ֨שֶׂם בֶּאֱד֜וֹם נְצִבִ֗ים בְּכָל־אֱדוֹם֙ שָׂ֣ם נְצִבִ֔ים וַיְהִ֥י כָל־אֱד֖וֹם עֲבָדִ֣ים לְדָוִ֑ד וַיּ֤וֹשַׁע יְהוָה֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put in Edom garrisons; in all Edom he put garrisons, and became all Edom servants to David; and saved Yahweh David in all that he went.

en.L: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom he put garrisons, and all Edom became servants to David. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saved David wherever he went.
en.B: He stationed garrisons in Edom, throughout all Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave David victory wherever he went.
en.R: David put groups of soldiers all through Edom, and all the Edomites came under his rule. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made David win wherever he went.

fr.L: Et il mit des garnisons en Édom ; dans tout Édom il mit des garnisons, et tout Édom devint serviteur de David. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sauva David partout où il alla.
fr.B: Il plaça des garnisons en Édom, dans tout Édom, et tous les Édomites furent soumis à David. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} donna la victoire à David partout où il alla.
fr.R: David a installé des groupes de soldats dans tout Édom, et tous les Édomites sont passés sous son autorité. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait gagner David partout où il allait.

decisions.choice: Edom becomes subject to Israel
decisions.reason: Edom, the descendants of Esau, now serves the line of Jacob, as Genesis 25:23 and 27:29, 40 had said, and as Balaam foresaw (Numbers 24:18). Edom stayed under Judah's rule until the days of Jehoram (2 Kings 8:20-22).

decisions.choice: garrisons repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says it twice, "in Edom ... in all Edom", stressing that David's posts covered the whole land.

decisions.choice: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The refrain of verse 6 is repeated: every victory is the LORD's gift.

decisions.choice: gave David victory (Balanced); made David win (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ דָּוִ֖ד עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י דָוִ֗ד עֹשֶׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְכָל־עַמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And reigned David over all Israel, and was David doing justice and righteousness for all his people.

en.L: And David reigned over all Israel, and David was doing justice and righteousness for all his people.
en.B: So David reigned over all Israel, and he did what was just and right for all his people.
en.R: David ruled over all Israel. He was fair to all his people and did what was right for them.

fr.L: Et David régna sur tout Israël, et David pratiquait le droit et la justice pour tout son peuple.
fr.B: David régna donc sur tout Israël, et il faisait ce qui était juste et droit pour tout son peuple.
fr.R: David a régné sur tout Israël. Il était juste envers tout son peuple et il faisait ce qui était bien pour eux.

decisions.choice: doing justice and righteousness: ruling fairly and rightly
decisions.reason: The pair describes the ideal king (Jeremiah 22:15; 23:5; Psalm 72:1-2): fair judgments in court and right dealing that protects the weak. It is the same pair the LORD loves (Psalm 33:5).

decisions.choice: was doing: an ongoing practice
decisions.reason: The verb "was" with a participle describes the steady pattern of David's rule, not a single act.

decisions.choice: a summary of David's reign, opening the list of officials
decisions.reason: The wars are summed up, and the verse turns to how David governed at home; verses 16-18 name the men who served him.

decisions.choice: what was just and right (Balanced); fair ... what was right (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two nouns. Balanced and Readable use adjectives, which say the same thing in natural English.

source.text: וְיוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֖ה עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־אֲחִיל֖וּד מַזְכִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joab son of Zeruiah [was] over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] recorder,

en.L: And Joab son of Zeruiah [was] over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] recorder,
en.B: Joab son of Zeruiah was commander of the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
en.R: Joab son of Zeruiah was the army commander. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the royal records.

fr.L: Et Joab fils de Tserouya [était] sur l’armée, et Josaphat fils d’Ahiloud [était] chancelier,
fr.B: Joab fils de Tserouya était chef de l’armée ; Josaphat fils d’Ahiloud était chancelier ;
fr.R: Joab fils de Tserouya était le chef de l’armée. Josaphat fils d’Ahiloud tenait les archives du royaume.

decisions.choice: Joab son of Zeruiah: David's nephew and commander
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her son Joab led David's army for most of his reign (2:13; 11:1; 20:23). Joab won the post at the taking of Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 11:6).

decisions.choice: recorder: the official who kept the royal records and perhaps announced the king's decisions
decisions.reason: The title comes from the verb "remember": literally "one who causes to remember". He seems to have kept the state's records and reminded the king of business. The same office appears under Solomon (1 Kings 4:3) and Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18; Isaiah 36:3).

decisions.choice: one list of officials across verses 16-18
decisions.reason: The list of David's officials is a series of short clauses joined by "and", running on to the end of verse 18. 2 Samuel 20:23-26 gives a later form of the same list.

decisions.choice: commander of the army (Balanced); army commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Over the army" means in command of it; Balanced and Readable use the usual title for this office in these books.

decisions.choice: chancelier (L, B); tenait les archives du royaume (R)
decisions.reason: The official kept the royal records and announced the king's decisions (m2); "chancelier" names such a court office in French, and Readable says what he did.

source.text: וְצָד֧וֹק בֶּן־אֲחִיט֛וּב וַאֲחִימֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִ֑ים וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה סוֹפֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar [were] priests, and Seraiah [was] secretary,

en.L: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar [were] priests, and Seraiah [was] secretary,
en.B: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;
en.R: Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Seraiah was the royal secretary.

fr.L: et Sadok fils d’Ahitoub et Ahimélek fils d’Abiathar [étaient] prêtres, et Seraya [était] secrétaire,
fr.B: Sadok fils d’Ahitoub et Ahimélek fils d’Abiathar étaient prêtres ; Seraya était secrétaire ;
fr.R: Sadok fils d’Ahitoub et Ahimélek fils d’Abiathar étaient prêtres. Seraya était le secrétaire du roi.

decisions.choice: Ahimelech son of Abiathar
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Abiathar is the son of Ahimelech (1 Samuel 22:20), and Zadok and Abiathar are David's two priests (15:24-35; 20:25). 1 Chronicles 18:16 reads "Abimelech son of Abiathar", and 1 Chronicles 24:6 also has "Ahimelech son of Abiathar". Either the names were reversed in copying, so that the text first read "Abiathar son of Ahimelech", or Abiathar had a son named after his grandfather who served with him. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Zadok son of Ahitub: a priest of Aaron's line
decisions.reason: Zadok first appears here. 1 Chronicles 5:34 traces him through Eleazar son of Aaron; his family served as chief priests from Solomon's reign onward (1 Kings 2:35).

decisions.choice: Seraiah the secretary: the royal scribe
decisions.reason: The secretary wrote and kept the king's letters and records of state. The same man may be Sheva (20:25), Shavsha (1 Chronicles 18:16) and Shisha (1 Kings 4:3); the name is spelled differently in each list.

decisions.choice: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: Readable adds "royal" so that the reader knows this was a high office at the king's court.

source.text: וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וְהַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֑י וּבְנֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד כֹּהֲנִ֥ים הָיֽוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethite and the Pelethite, and [the] sons of David priests were.

en.L: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were priests.
en.B: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.
en.R: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Cherethites and the Pelethites, who were the king's bodyguard. And David's sons were priests.

fr.L: et Benaya fils de Yehoyada et les Kéréthiens et les Péléthiens ; et les fils de David étaient prêtres.
fr.B: Benaya fils de Yehoyada commandait les Kéréthiens et les Péléthiens ; et les fils de David étaient prêtres.
fr.R: Benaya fils de Yehoyada était le chef des Kéréthiens et des Péléthiens, qui formaient la garde du roi. Et les fils de David étaient prêtres.

decisions.choice: Benaiah was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites
alternatives: Benaiah, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites (as a separate group)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply joins Benaiah "and the Cherethites and the Pelethites" with no verb or title. The parallel list in 20:23 and 1 Chronicles 18:17 say Benaiah was "over" them, and that is the sense here.

decisions.choice: Cherethites and Pelethites: foreign soldiers who formed the king's guard
decisions.reason: The Cherethites were a people of the Philistine coast linked with Crete (1 Samuel 30:14; Ezekiel 25:16; Zephaniah 2:5), and the Pelethites were probably Philistines too. They served David as a personal guard loyal to him alone (15:18; 20:7; 1 Kings 1:38, 44).

decisions.choice: David's sons were priests
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for priest, the same as in verse 17. It is surprising, since priests came from the family of Aaron (Numbers 3:10). David's sons may have served in a priestly role connected with the king, as David himself wore the ephod and offered sacrifices (6:14, 17-18) and Ira the Jairite was "priest to David" (20:26). 1 Chronicles 18:17 says instead that David's sons were "the chief officials at the king's side", and the Greek translation calls them "court officials"; this may mean the word here has a wider sense, such as chief ministers (compare 1 Kings 4:5). The word is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: was over (Balanced); was in charge of (Readable)
decisions.reason: Following meaning decision m1, Balanced and Readable supply the link between Benaiah and the guard. Readable also says who the Cherethites and Pelethites were.
